title: Rigid many-one degrees contain infinite antichains of $1$-degrees
summary: Odifreddi asked whether every non-irreducible many-one degree must contain an infinite antichain of one-one degrees. Positive answers are known for computably enumerable many-one degrees (Degtev) and, more recently, for many-one degrees admitting a $Δ^0_2$ representative (Batyrshin). In this note we isolate a rigidity principle behind these phenomena. Call a set $A\subseteqω$ \emph{$m$-rigid} if every total computable $m$-autoreduction of $A$ is eventually the identity.
